_README: Gertrud (job witchfinale, 4 Nov 2026). The old lady the witch turns into on 12 Dec. EVERY spoken line is here with an id, so Marius can re-record it. VOICE: the CapCut grandma voice (same export/split/import flow as the townspeople, memory capcut-townsperson-voices). The CapCut voice name is noted in voice.capcutName once it is applied. Until a recording exists the game speaks the line with the browser voice (placeholder) and always shows the caption. A recording is picked up by dropping voice/gertrud/<id>.m4a (no code change). Gift notes (gifts.*.note) are WRITTEN notes, not spoken.

voice.capcutName: TBD (note the exact CapCut voice when applied)
voice.status: placeholder: browser TTS, no recording yet
voice.recordWith: recording studio page; one take per id; export as the 'gertrud' track

b1.t: Today is the day. Or it is not. I have been wrong about dates before, I admit it.

b2_tin.t: You have Mamma's tin. It rattles like a small, brave drum. Keep it dry.

b2_no.t: No tin. No Mamma's baking. I would go down anyway, but I would bring a very long stick.

b3.t: She is down the stairs. She is bigger than she was. Every cookie she stole is in there somewhere. The old lantern is already in your hand, I put it there while you were not looking. Please do not be hit.

sp1.t: Look. The green is leaving her, like water out of a bath. I do not know where it goes.

sp2.t: Oh. Oh, my. Why is it so dark in here? And why am I standing next to a cauldron?

sp3.t: I remember a bag of sugar. Then a lot of cackling. Was that me? That was me, wasn't it.

sp4_tin.t: Is that a tin? Oh, honey. It smells of ginger and candle smoke. It smells like home. Sugar-free, in a way. Made with the first candle. Well, I never.

sp4_no.t: Did somebody bring cookies? No. Of course not. I ate them all, didn't I.

sp5.t: Your mother's cookies. Every single box. I thought they were meant for me. There was a name on them. There was YOUR name on them. I am so, so sorry.

sp6.t: Something just left this room and went up through the floor. Warm. The whole valley feels warmer. I do not know what it was. I only know I felt it.

sp7.t: My name is Gertrud, by the way. I will leave something at your door tomorrow, and the day after. Do not you dare say no. Now. Who tiled this floor?

g1.t: Sit down, honey. I am going to tell you something about myself. I am American.

g2.t: That is why the broom was never really my thing. Back home, a girl keeps something in the kitchen drawer for the nights when the woods get loud.

g3.t: It is a revolver. It was my grandfather's. I have held onto it since the green went away, and I would feel better if it lived with you.

g4.t: Listen to me. You never point it at anyone who is not out there in the dark wanting to hurt you. Never at a child. Never at a neighbor. And the police in this town are very, very quick.

g5.t: It is loud, too. Everything in the woods will hear it, and some of them will come closer. Do you understand?

g5b.t: I do not like this. But I like her, and I do not know the woods well enough to argue.

g6.t: Good. Six bullets in it, and a few spare. I will find you more in time. Nobody else around here sells them. That is how I like it.

t0.t: Oh! A visitor. Come in, come in, and mind the trapdoor. I never did find out who built that.

t1.t: I bake with the sugar-free flour now. It tastes like regret, but it keeps me human.

t2.t: The broom? I use it for sweeping now. Imagine that. A broom, for sweeping.

t3.t: Your mother writes the loveliest letters. I read them out loud to the cat. I do not have a cat. Maybe I have a cat.

t4.t: I used to be a witch, you know. Not by choice. Gosh, the paperwork.

t5.t: Have you eaten? Eat something green. Not the green cookies. The OTHER green.

t6.t: Did the basket arrive at your door? Good. Do not let it get cold, honey.

tk.t: Oh, you are welcome, honey. That is the nicest thing anyone has said to me since nineteen sixty-one.

tk2.t: You thanked me already today. Now go and be warm somewhere.

pre.t: Come back tomorrow, dear. I need to find my glasses, and my dignity, and I do not think they are in the same place.

gifts._README: One basket per advent day 13..24 at Chris's front door, one per player per day (kv-story-v1 once-key gertrudGift:<day>). From 25 Dec the table repeats by real date (still one a day). Every item has a use and every stack has a note saying what for. 'guns' rows are given only if that gun was never given before (once-key gertrudGun:<id>). Ammo rows only if the player owns that gun. Animal foods feed animals for Koselig (daily cap in __SPIRIT, nothing sells).

13.title: Lucia buns
13.note:
Lucia buns, six of them, with saffron. Eat one now and one for each of the others.
And 30 carrots for the deer down by the river. They look thin. Hold one out and stand very still.
- Gertrud

14.title: Carrot cake and a lot of carrots
14.note:
A carrot cake, because I had too many carrots.
So here are 60 more. Go and feed the deer, the horses, anyone with ears.
- Gertrud

15.title: Ginger and fish
15.note:
Pepperkaker. The sugar-free kind. Be brave.
And fish for the cats. The ones behind the shops look like they have opinions about your last fish.
- Gertrud

16.title: Krumkake and bones
16.note:
Krumkake, rolled while still warm. Do not tell anyone about the cone trick.
Dog treats for any dog that will have them.
And six more bullets for the revolver. Only for the dark, honey.
- Gertrud

17.title: Julekake and apples
17.note:
A julekake with raisins. Slice it thin and share it.
Twenty apples for the horses. Flat hand, they are all fingers about it.
- Gertrud

18.title: Lefse and nuts
18.note:
Lefse, butter and sugar-free sugar. It works better than it sounds.
Nuts for the squirrels. They talk about you.
- Gertrud

19.title: A rifle from home
19.note:
Skillingsboller, warm.
Seeds for the little birds on the fence.
And my father's hunting rifle, from my homeland. It is for the big dark things in the woods, never for anyone who walks on two legs and is not trying to eat you. Keep it clean.
- Gertrud

20.title: Risgrot and moss
20.note:
Risgrot, with the almond hidden in it. Whoever finds it gets a wish. Do not fight over it.
Reindeer moss for the reindeer, up where it is cold.
- Gertrud

21.title: Winter solstice supplies
21.note:
Vafler, with sour cream and jam.
Carrots again. You have no idea how many carrots one old lady can end up with.
And four shells for the shotgun, in case a long night gets longer.
- Gertrud

22.title: A shotgun, as promised
22.note:
More pepperkaker, and fish for the cats.
And the Hagle, a double-barrel. It is heavy, it is loud, it is very much from my homeland. Two barrels. Make them count. Never near a child.
- Gertrud

23.title: Gingerbread day
23.note:
Hot cocoa for the baking. The gingerbread house wants your whole heart, and a little cocoa.
Nuts and treats for whoever is waiting outside.
- Gertrud

24.title: Julaften
24.note:
Merry Christmas, honey. A julekake, buns, apples for the horses and carrots for the deer, so everyone in the valley eats tonight.
Thank you for forgiving an old witch.
- Gertrud

pool.note:
Pepperkaker, and carrots for the deer. Same as ever.
- Gertrud

Buns for you, fish for the cats behind the shops.
- Gertrud

Carrot cake, and apples for the horses.
- Gertrud

Krumkake, and treats for the dogs.
- Gertrud

Lefse, and nuts for the squirrels.
- Gertrud

Vafler, and seeds for the little birds.
- Gertrud
